1

 Judgment

This appeal is filed at the instance of the claimant in O.P. (MV) No.637 of 2019 before the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Kalpetta, and seeks to challenge the fixation of the notional income at Rs.10,000/- by the impugned award.
The accident occurred on 05.07.2019 when the claimant was aged 68 years.
2. I have heard Sri. A.R. Nimod, the learned counsel for the claimant, as well as Sri. P.K. Manoj Kumar, the learned counsel for the insurance company.
3. This Court notices that the claimant was pointed out to be a coolie worker earning an amount of Rs.20,000/- per month before the Tribunal.
However, it has been categorically recorded in the impugned award that no evidence whatsoever was adduced by the claimant to show or to prove the vocation as well as income.
However, in that view of the matter, I am of the opinion that the notional income requires to be fixed on an estimate basis as done by the Tribunal.

Though the learned counsel for the claimant would contend that, insofar as the claimant was pointed out to be a coolie worker, he was entitled to fixation of notional income with reference to the notifications 2025:KER:93567 issued under the Minimum Wages Act,1948, since the vocation of the claimant has not been established in accordance with law, I am of the opinion that the claimant is not entitled to succeed on this ground, and only question that arises is whether the amount fixed by the Tribunal requires any tinkering in this appeal.
This Court notices that the accident has taken place in the year 2019.

With reference to the principles laid down by the Apex Court in Ramachandrappa V. Manager,
Royal Sundaram Alliance Insurance Company Ltd. [(2011) 13 SCC 236], the notional income for the afore mentioned year needs to be fixed at 12,000/-, and to that extent, the award of the Tribunal requires to be re-fixed, and I do so.
4.

sentences.text: Though Sri. A.R. Nimod, the learned counsel for the claimant, would contend that the award passed by the Tribunal on the other grounds also falls on the lower side, on perusal of the award, I notice that with reference to other heads, including the claims under "Pain and Sufferings", "Loss of amenities", etc., reasonable amounts have already been awarded by the Tribunal considering the nature of the injuries as certified in Ext.C1 - Medical Certificate.

In such circumstances, I am of the opinion that the award of the Tribunal requires to be sustained, but for 2025:KER:93567 the modifications with respect to the notional income as noticed above.

In the result, this appeal is partly allowed, modifying the 2025:KER:93567 impugned award,
entitling the appellant to get an additional amount of Rs.4,02,700/- (Rupees Four Lakhs Two Thousand and Seven Hundred only), along with the amounts already awarded by the Tribunal, to be paid by the 2 nd respondent - Insurance Company.
Needless to say, all other findings and directions of the Tribunal in the impugned award, including the rate of interest, will remain unaltered.
